source.title: ScopeSAE: Model-Scope Feature Discovery with Interpretable Layer Selection
source.authors: Qing-Wen Zeng; Ze-Hao Fu; Shu-Yu Meng; Ling-Han Huang; Jia-Yi Zhang; Chenglin Wu; Ling Chen; Hua-Ming Chen

page_placements.theme: Retaining reconstruction error is not uniformly beneficial

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures how SAE reconstructions affect next-token cross-entropy and tests interventions on the reconstruction residual. It does not use the original study’s measurements of linear predictability or error scaling across SAE sizes.
record.gate_note: The paper reports reconstruction-versus-original cross-entropy results, which bear on V3’s claim about reconstruction harming model loss. It does not compare reconstructions with random errors of matched size. Residual-gradient geometry and residual-addback results are recorded as findings about the subject, but do not measure the specific properties in V1, V2, V4, or V5.
record.test_reason: The study reports next-token cross-entropy when SAE reconstructions replace activations. Baselines (TopK, RouteSAE, per-layer TopK) raise CE, while ScopeSAE lowers it on four models. This bears on V3 in a new setting (gradient-selected, target-relative writeback). No matched-size random-error baseline is reported, so V3's 'pathological' comparison itself is not run. No result bears on V1, V2, V4, V5 or V6.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely right. The authors conclude that ScopeSAE reconstructions yield lower CE than the original activations because the sparse bottleneck removes prediction-orthogonal residual components. They attribute this to the prediction-relevant subspace together with the reconstruction objective, not to architecture or selection alone. They also report that the reduction is concentrated on tokens the model already predicts correctly.
record.recipe_differences: The paper proposes ScopeSAE, a TopK SAE trained on token-layer states selected by normalized gradient attribution, with token-wise normalization and a normalized reconstruction objective. It is not a reproduction of the original study’s dark-matter measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: The reconstruction effect varies with selection target and evaluation token subset; it disappears after decoder KL fine-tuning. Across the reported model family/scale, the DeltaCE sign remains negative.

fits_no_version.finding: The ScopeSAE residual aligns with the prediction gradient below chance (0.0103 vs 0.0176). Adding back its gradient-perpendicular part raises CE by +0.330; adding back the parallel part lowers CE by −0.111.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For a prediction-selected SAE, the reconstruction error is mostly prediction-orthogonal, and its orthogonal component worsens next-token loss when restored.

record.problems: The main experiments use Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct; the paper reports no formal error bars for most results, although Appendix O gives mean ± std over three seeds for selection-target comparisons. It does not compare SAE errors against random errors of matched size, and the residual decomposition is defined relative to prediction gradients rather than input-linear predictability.
record.rows_left_out: Not included: the paper’s feature steering win rates and feature-quality metrics, which do not directly measure reconstruction-error effects; the full per-layer fixed-SAE DeltaCE sweep in Appendix O, which is summarized in the text as positive at every tested layer; and the additional residual-intervention sweeps in Appendix G, which extend rather than alter the gradient-parallel/perpendicular finding recorded here.

untested.parts: No linear prediction of the error from the input activation.
No per-token error-norm prediction across SAE sizes, and no test of shared failure contexts or scaling.
No comparison of reconstruction-induced CE change against random errors of matched norm.
The residual is split by prediction-gradient direction, not into linear and nonlinear parts; learnability of either part is not tested.
No circuit or steering analysis with versus without the error term.
No test of whether error shrinks with architecture or training; end-to-end SAEs are discussed only, not trained.

missing.what: Selection rule routed over independently trained per-layer TopK SAEs: DeltaCE +0.081; best single-layer TopK +0.070
Selection-mechanism ablation DeltaCE: activation patching −0.117, full-state ablation +0.107
ScopeSAE DeltaCE across corpus and budget: OWT2 100M −0.197, OWT2 300M −0.217, FineWeb 100M −0.139, FineWeb 300M −0.156
Per-layer TopK DeltaCE values L0–L15 (+0.070 to +0.389). The record declares these as summarized only, but the exact numbers are available.

record.verdict_notes: The reversal arises under a non-standard substitution: the writeback layer is chosen per token using gradients of the target, or of the predicted token in the control. This is why it is scored as limits_scope rather than challenges for V3, which concerns standard fixed-layer substitution versus random errors. The study never frames its results in terms of SAE dark matter.

versions.untested_parts: No test of whether a large share of the error vector is a linear function of the input activation.
No comparison of per-token error norms across SAE sizes or whether larger and smaller SAEs fail on the same contexts.
The study does not compare reconstruction-induced loss changes with random errors of the same size.

The residual is decomposed relative to prediction-gradient directions, not into input-linearly-predictable and nonlinear parts; the study does not test whether either part is learnable by further dictionary learning.
No test of circuits or steering analyses with versus without the SAE error term.

The paper compares SAE methods and includes decoder KL fine-tuning, but does not directly measure whether dark matter is chiefly a training artifact or shrinks under better architectures or end-to-end training.

relationships.condition: ScopeSAE: gradient-attributed per-token layer selection with target-relative writeback, on Llama-3.2-1B/3.1-8B and Qwen2.5-0.5B/7B
relationships.reason: Substituting reconstructions lowers CE rather than harming it (r2, r5, r6, r12–r15). The reversal sits on ŷ=y tokens (r8, r10) and depends on the selection and objective; no random-error baseline is reported.
relationships.display_finding: Reconstruction substitution lowered cross-entropy on tokens where predictions matched targets, depending on layer selection and the training objective; no random-error comparison was reported.

relation.reason: Its reconstruction-writeback experiments bear directly on V3's loss-harm premise, although the matched-random comparison remains untested.

tranche.reason: Reports reconstruction-writeback loss in a new setting using prediction-relevant token-layer selection and a normalized reconstruction objective.
